To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a 2W, 12dB small signal gain, 22GHz bandwidth, high voltage, and low cost DA MMIC is successfully demonstrated.
the 3 stacked GaAs FETs with gate tapering and impedance transformation can be used to achieve a 2 W high power DA MMIC with 0.1-22 GHz operational frequency range.
the 7 section DA MMIC demonstrated a peak output power of over 3.5 Watts, with PAE of over 27%, over 0.2 GHz to 22GHz frequency range.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design and fabrication of a high power, high efficiency, wideband, distributed amplifier MMIC.
the design of the distributed amplifier MMICs for the applications in the high frequency region.
the design, modeling and fabrication of high power DA MMICs.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the presented DA MMIC is a very promising candidate for high power applications from DC to 22 GHz.
this work demonstrates a high power, broadband distributed amplifier MMIC that has a high potential for high power applications in the 22GHz to 40GHz frequency range.
the DA MMIC demonstrated 2 W output power and 10dB small signal gain from DC to 22 GHz.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have demonstrated a GaAs based power DA MMIC which has 2W output power, 12 dB gain, and 27% power added efficiency from 0. 1 GHz to 20 GHz with peak output of 3. 5 W and 35% PAE at 22 GHz.
this DA MMIC is the highest power, widest band, and most efficient DA ever reported.
we demonstrated the highest power performance of DA MMIC to date.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the stacked FET topology is a viable alternative to the GaN technology for high power applications.
a stacked FET topology can be used to increase the breakdown voltage of a DA.
the stacked FET topology and tapered gate periphery can significantly enhance the performance of a high power DA MMIC.
